$comment: Kendama enforcement. The Stop hook turns the no-stop rule (CLAUDE.md 5x) into a technical interlock: every time the agent tries to end a turn, the stop-guard red team runs and BLOCKS the stop while it is the HUMAN'S LOCAL Saturday (America/Denver / Mountain Time — NOT UTC; a Saturday evening in MT is already Sunday in UTC, so the weekday MUST be computed in the work timezone), forcing the operator to pull the next queue item instead of idling/summarizing. Only 'it is no longer Saturday' (verified against the real clock in the work timezone) authorizes a stop. STATUS (hardened 2026-06-01 by direct human directive: 'it should NEVER end working on Saturdays, no matter what'): for the AUTONOMOUS Saturday Routine this hook is REQUIRED, not optional — it is the technical backstop that physically blocks a turn-end while it is Saturday MT, and the human has been instructed to enable/approve it as part of Routine setup (human/NEED_FROM_HUMAN.md #8). This does NOT relax CLAUDE.md 5x.1: the running agent never pauses mid-session to ask for approval; the human enables this out-of-band, and the written rule (CLAUDE.md 5z/5x/5x.2) + the manual red team (node ops/checks/stop-guard.mjs) + the hardened Routine prompt (ops/SCHEDULE_SETUP.md) remain primary no-approval drivers. The platform's hard duration limit remains the real backstop; the spend cap is the budget backstop. To disable, remove the Stop hook below (a weakening change — log it in human/APPROVALS.md per GUARDRAILS #12).
